title: 4D Light-sheet Imaging of Zebrafish Cardiac Contraction
protocol: Maintain and breed adult zebrafish through standard care and breeding procedures.
Transfer embryos at 1 day post-fertilization (dpf) to E3 water with 0.2 mM PTU to prevent pigment formation.
Replace the medium with fresh E3 water containing PTU every day until LSM imaging.
Image embryos or larvae with a stereo microscope at desired timepoints between 0 and 7 dpf.
Prepare segmented fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP) tubes with a 2 mm inner diameter for embedding zebrafish larvae under the LSM system.
Transfer fish to a 150 mg/L tricaine solution starting from 3 dpf.
Prepare 0.8% low-melting agarose with 150 mg/L tricaine and allow it to cool to room temperature.
Use a transfer pipette to move anesthetized fish into the cooled agarose solution.
Mount the fish in FEP tubes using a transfer pipette.

Construct an in-house LSM system based on a cylindrical lens using continuous-wave diode-pumped solid-state (DPSS) laser systems at specific wavelengths such as 473 nm and 532 nm as illumination sources.
Customize LabVIEW control codes for the synchronization of translational sample stage, light-sheet illumination, and exposure of sCMOS camera to capture image sequences.
Dilute fluorescent beads having the diameter of 0.53 µm to a concentration of 1: 1.5 x 10^5 using 0.8 % low-melting agarose.
Transfer the diluted bead solution to the segmented FEP tube.
Image the beads using the LSM system and measure the point spread function (PSF) across the entire sample.
Validate the spatial resolution and system alignment based on the PSF measurement.
Attach the FEP tube with mounted zebrafish larva securely to the motorized sample stage.
Submerge the tubes into the sample chamber filled with E3 water.
Rotate the zebrafish larva to take images from the ventral side.
Adjust all essential settings in the customized LabVIEW control program, including exposure time of 5 ms and desired region of interest.
Configure the number of image sequences and frames.
Power on the laser.
Initiate LSM imaging of the sample.
Record 300 frames as a 2D image sequence to cover 3-5 cardiac cycles of the larva with a framerate of 200 frames/second.
Move the larva at the step size of 1 µm across the light-sheet illumination.
Repeat the process until the whole heart is covered.
Open the file test_Parallel.m in MATLAB.
Specify the folder location where the raw image sequences are stored in the variable "baseDir".
Assign the variable "numOfSlice" with the total number of image sequences (typically 100-150).
Assign the variable "numOfImage" with the number of images (typically 300-500) in each sequence.
Inspect the image sequence showing the middle plane of the zebrafish heart.
Identify the frame numbers of the first systole and assign it to the variable systolicPoint_1st.
Identify the frame numbers of the fourth systole and assign it to the variable systolicPoint_4th.
Click on Run to start the process.
Check the results in the output folder.
Download the 3DeeCellTracker package and set up the Python environment.

Download ITK-SNAP annotation software and use it to manually label the 3D heart image at two selected timepoints: one during ventricular diastole and the other during ventricular systole, creating training and validation datasets.
Run the 3DeeCellTracker training program in Python and initialize the noise_level(100), folder_path, and model parameters in TrainingUNet3D function to set up the predefined 3D U-Net model.
Use the imageDimConverter.m program in MATLAB to convert and rename the training and validation dataset to the proper format for loading.
Load the training and validation datasets using trainer.load_dataset().
Draw the dataset using trainer.draw_dataset().
Run the first part of the 3DeeCellTracker tracking program.
Initialize image parameters for characterizing image dimensions.
Select the U-Net model for cell segmentation.
Employ FFN+ PR-GLS for cell registration.
Store data, models, and results in automatically created folders.
Use the imageDimConverter.m program to convert and rename all 3D heart images.
Transfer converted images to the data folder created previously.
Run the second part of the 3DeeCellTracker program to start segmentation.
Compare the segmentation result with the raw image for each segment.
Perform manual correction if incorrect segmentation is found.
Move corrected segmentation to the "/manual_vol1" folder.
Run the third part of the 3DeeCellTracker program to segment all images.
Use Amira to perform a visual assessment of tracking outcomes by comparing the positions of tracked cells with their corresponding raw images.
Recommence the procedure from step 6.6 if test results are not satisfying.
Employ an alternative machine learning model for segmentation or cell registration.
Re-initiate the tracking process after changing the model.
Set the format of data of cell labels as a 16-bit image in the tracking program to address the label limitation issue.
Use the "separateTrackingResults.py" program to post-process the cell labels and separate cells with the same labels based on their physical location, assigning each cell a different label.
Manually validate the data from previous steps.
Select cells with consistent image intensity across all volumes (about 500 cells out of approximately 600).
Use cellLabelsToObj.ipynb script to generate a surface mesh for each individual cell through 3D Slicer software.
Assign a unique color code to each cell.
Export each 3D model as a single .obj file accompanied by a .mtl file describing the cell label.
Import the models into Unity using an educational license.
Apply customized C# scripts to the models and user-interface elements for 4D visualization and interactive analysis.
Perform VR interaction following specified steps.
Interact with the models in virtual reality (VR).
Select up to two cells at a time and view their trajectories, velocities, volumes, surface areas, and relative distances.
Choose a specific time point in the data to analyze outputs of selected cells.
Freeze the dynamic model to focus on selected cells and their outputs.
Modulate contrast between selected cells and surrounding cells in the model.
